title: Ruleform conciliation graph — labbook and API playbook
body:
Purpose

This is my labbook for the "Ruleform conciliation graph" idea: a tiny system that accepts diverse ingress rule representations from multiple sources (tenant settings, team overrides, platform defaults, legacy NGINX-style fragments, operator fences) and reconciles them into a canonical routing + QoS policy that the runtime compiler can consume.

Why we need it

Context: we have multiple tenants each shipping small policy fragments: path rewrites, weight-based traffic splits, region-specific allow/deny constraints, and transform hooks. Current ad-hoc merging in the ingress layer causes surprising overrides (tenant A's rule shadowing platform-level safety), brittle ordering dependencies, and a lack of provenance for runtime fallbacks. The conciliation graph aims to:
- Capture provenance (where did this rule come from)
- Normalize different shapes to a common intermediate representation (IR)
- Apply deterministic conciliation rules (override, merge, decouple)
- Emit a compiler-friendly manifest (batches of atomic routing rules + fallbacks)

High level components (sketch)

[ingestor] --> [normalizer] --> [conciliation-engine (graph model)] --> [policy-compiler] --> [runtime]
                         |
                         v
                     [audit-store]

- ingestor: HTTP webhook + pullers for Confluence/Jira/ticket metadata + tenant API (push). Pullers will also import older NGINX-like fragments (text) via a parser.
- normalizer: runs a set of adapters that convert vendor/legacy shapes into a small IR. Handles canonicalization (path suffixes, method lists, header match normal forms).
- conciliation-engine: core. A directed graph where nodes are rule fragments (with provenance, priority, TTL, scope). Edges express relationships: overrides, binds-to, dependent-on. The engine runs graph transforms (conflict detection, merge, rewrite rules) and emits an ordered DAG of atomic actions.
- policy-compiler: takes DAG and compiles to runtime unit(s): envoy route configs, runtime prewarm directives, safety fences.
- audit-store: append-only store of decisions, diffs, fingerprints for later RCA.

Key invariants

- Deterministic output: given same inputs + timestamps produce identical compiled manifest.
- Explainability: each final atomic rule must map back to 1..N source fragments and a named conciliation step.
- Minimal surprise: platform safety fences always produce hard denies unless explicitly relaxed by an authorized override.

IR shape (textual)

Example of normalized fragment (pseudo-JSON inside document):

{
  "fragment_id": "tenant-453/path-split-1",
  "source": "tenant-api",
  "priority": 100,
  "scope": "tenant:453",
  "match": {"path_prefix": "/billing", "methods": ["GET","POST"]},
  "actions": [{"type": "route", "target": "svc-billing-v2", "weight": 80}, {"type":"route","target":"svc-billing-v1","weight":20}],
  "constraints": [{"region": "eu-west-1"}],
  "metadata": {"created_by":"alice@example.com","ticket":"JIRA-231"}
}

Conciliation graph node model (conceptual):
- node_id (string)
- fragment_ref (string)
- semantic_tags (list) e.g. ["split","rewrite","deny"]
- effective_priority (int) = base_priority +/- adjustments
- edges: override_of, depends_on, binds_with

Conciliation rules (examples)

1) Priority-merge: if two fragments target the same match and are both active, sort by effective_priority then source_trust_score, then fragment_age. If equal, tie-break on fragment_id hash.

2) Safety fence: platform-deny fragments (tag: "platform-safety") always beat tenant fragments unless tenant fragment carries an explicit signed relaxation token. Record any relaxations in audit-store.

3) Split normalization: when multiple splits overlap, normalize to an explicit weight matrix across named targets. If weights conflict, prefer higher priority fragment but log a reconciliation event.

4) Rewrite chaining: path rewrites are chained left-to-right based on "binds_with" edges; detect potential infinite loops and reject with explanation.

Example API surfaces

1) POST /v1/rule-forms/import 
- accepts arbitrary vendor shape + optional source metadata. Returns fragment_id and status (accepted|rejected|needs-review)

Request body example (multipart/json):
{"source": "nginx-fragment", "payload":"server { location /x { proxy_pass http://svc; } }", "owner":"connie@acme"}

2) GET /v1/conciliation/plan?scope=tenant:453&preview=true
- returns the planned DAG, human-readable explanations, diff vs. current runtime manifest.

3) POST /v1/conciliation/apply?dry_run=false
- applies compiled manifest to target environment(s) (staging, prod). Returns operation id and audit link.

4) GET /v1/conciliation/explain?atomic_id=abc123
- returns provenance chain: list of fragment_ids, applied ruleset names, and rulebook steps that led to this atomic rule.

Config sketch (YAML-like in text)

conciliator:
  concurrency: 4
  default_priority: 50
  source_trust_scores:
    platform: 100
    tenant: 50
    operator: 80
  safety_policy:
    enforce_platform_denies: true
    signed_relaxation_required: true
  storage:
    audit: s3://redwood-psc/conciliation-audit
    graph: dgraph://conciliation-main

Operational concerns / open questions

- Performance: graph transforms need to be bounded. We should run incremental conciliation on deltas rather than full graph rebuilds. Implement an incremental dependency-tracking index (per fragment change -> touched subgraph).
- Backwards compatibility: runtime expects Envoy route tables. Compiler must be able to emit both v1 and v2 shapes while we migrate. Add versioned manifests and a short grace period.
- Rollout strategy: canary compile + traffic-shadowing vs direct replace. Tie into Redwood Console rollouts to use canary percentages and automatic rollback on error signals.
- Security: signed relaxation tokens (HMAC with KMS) — need a rotation model and audit. Who can sign? RBAC hook with identity provider.
- Conflict resolution policy: should platform offer a self-serve UI for tenants to see conflicts and propose merges, or should conciliation be fully automated with operator review baked into certain thresholds? Lean towards automated with human-in-the-loop for high-impact conflicts.

Prototype tasks (next steps)

- [ ] implement simple normalizer for three shapes: tenant-api, nginx-fragment, ingress-helm-values. (Connor)
- [ ] minimal conciliation-engine: priority sort + override detection + provenance recording (MVP: no graph DB; in-memory DAG persisted as JSON). (me)
- [ ] compiler: emit envoy route config with annotation fields mapping to provenance (Maya)
- [ ] audit UI: simple table view for operation id -> fragments -> diffs (ops)
- [ ] load tests: simulated 10k fragments/day ingest, 1k tenants, measure conciliation latency.

Notes / heuristics I keep thinking about

- Trust scores are political; make them config and expose safe defaults.
- Keep the audit-store append-only; make the conciliation engine idempotent and keyed by digest so we can reapply safely.
- For debugging, offer a "replay" API: given a timestamp re-run conciliation with inputs <= t and produce same manifest. This will help RCA.

Fragment example (edge-case)

Tenant A: path /reports -> svc-reports (priority 60)
Platform: path /reports -> deny (platform-safety, priority 90)

Conciliation outcome: deny wins; tenant gets an explainable message including a link to request a signed relaxation via support flow.

Random brainstorm bullets (bits to not forget)

- fingerprinting: stable fingerprint for fragments to detect duplicates across imports.
- TTL on tenant fragments that are unattended -> auto-expire after X days with notification.
- cost center tags propagate to runtime for chargeback.
- allow "composition libraries": named rule bundles tenants can opt into instead of copy-paste.

References / related tickets

- JIRA-INF-827 (original platform safety scope)
- RFC-TR-62 (policy provenance schema)
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/462 (envoy metadata annotations)

Endnotes

This is intentionally rough. Goal is to capture the problem, some invariants, and a minimal API + IR to prototype. Will iterate after the normalizer MVP.
